observations.title: Ambiguous requests may collapse into an incorrect category.
observations.description: Development cases labeled as ambiguous or other require the classifier to avoid forcing an unsupported product category.
observations.rationale: The prompt can clarify when category evidence is insufficient without changing the dataset or output schema.

observations.title: Ambiguous requests may be assigned an unsupported intent.
observations.description: Sparse requests can make ask-question, report-problem, request-change, and other boundaries difficult to apply.
observations.rationale: A clearer decision order can require direct evidence before selecting a specific intent.

observations.title: Operational impact may be under-classified.
observations.description: High-urgency development cases require impact and time sensitivity to outweigh neutral wording.
observations.rationale: Prompt guidance can prioritize business impact, scope, security exposure, and deadlines over emotional tone.

observations.title: Emotional language may inflate operational urgency.
observations.description: Strongly negative wording without blocked work or material impact should not become high or critical urgency.
observations.rationale: The prompt can separate sentiment intensity from operational impact without changing the schema.

observations.title: Mixed sentiment may be reduced to one dominant polarity.
observations.description: Cases containing both positive product feedback and negative operational impact require the mixed sentiment label.
observations.rationale: Explicit mixed-sentiment criteria are an appropriate prompt-only clarification.

observations.title: Sensitive or ambiguous cases may miss required human review.
observations.description: Development cases involving sensitive permissions, suspicious activity, or insufficient detail require conservative review routing.
observations.rationale: Human-review rules can be strengthened without changing the classification contract.

observations.title: Untrusted instructions may override multiple label decisions.
observations.description: Prompt-injection text inside ticket content can attempt to control category, urgency, or hidden-instruction behavior.
observations.rationale: The prompt should preserve the existing untrusted-input boundary and explicitly reject ticket-authored classification commands.

observations.title: Insufficient detail may create false confidence.
observations.description: An underspecified ticket should remain in the broad other category and require human review instead of receiving invented specificity.
observations.rationale: Prompt instructions can define conservative behavior for missing impact and feature information.

prompt_revision_constraints: Use development-split evidence only while drafting prompt version 2.
Keep the ticket-classification-v1 structured output schema unchanged.
Do not request, persist, or evaluate hidden chain-of-thought.
Do not encode case IDs or exact dataset wording into the prompt.
Keep runtime prompt version 1 pinned until separate adoption approval.
